review_notes: Scope: Section 2.1, Table 2 Panels A and B, columns (2) and (3), are the principal 1963–1990 asymmetric-timeliness comparison. Actual and simulated returns are retained for both bad-news (Rit < 0) and good-news (Rit ≥ 0) regressions because the simulated-return fits provide the direct counterfactual comparison. Column (1) reports Basu (1997), columns (4)–(5) are a later-period reference, and the change-versus-level and cash-flow/accrual analyses are subsequent applications and are excluded. Table 2 Panel C column (2) is retained only as the full-sample actual return-on-earnings fit needed to generate simulated returns.

Table 1 describes Xit as scaled by stock price, while the equation-specific Table 2 note defines the retained Table 2 fits as scaled by firm market value nine months before fiscal year-end; used Table 2 definition for these fits and retained the Table 1 wording as contextual evidence.

Physical PDF page 20 was viewed. It confirms Panel A bad-news Rit < 0, Panel B good-news Rit ≥ 0, the three equation forms, and Table 2 note definitions. The text extraction renders the Panel B comparison sign as “-”; the physical page shows “≥”.
The source reports regression coefficient estimates and t-statistics but does not identify the estimator, inference correction, fixed effects, or weights for these fits.
